approach: Find the horizontal and vertical velocity parts, then use the equations of motion for the velocity and displacement after 2 s.

steps.text: Find the horizontal and vertical parts of the initial velocity.
Find the velocity components at t = 2 s.
steps.equation: vx = 40 m/s, vy = uy − gt = 40 − 20 = 20 m/s

steps.text: Combine the components for the speed and direction of the velocity.
steps.equation: v = √(40² + 20²) = 20√5 ≈ 44.72 m/s, about 26.6° above the horizontal

steps.text: Find the horizontal and vertical displacement at t = 2 s.
steps.equation: x = ux t = 80 m, y = uy t − ½gt² = 80 − 20 = 60 m

steps.text: Combine the displacement components for the magnitude and direction; this gives the final answer.
steps.equation: s = √(80² + 60²) = 100 m, about 36.9° above the horizontal

final_answer.value: (a) velocity ≈ 44.72 m/s at about 26.6° above the horizontal; (b) displacement = 100 m at about 36.9° above the horizontal

common_mistakes.text: Taking vy = uy + gt instead of uy − gt, as if gravity speeds the particle up, gives vy = 60 m/s and a wrong speed near 72.1 m/s.
